NONE: › a large group of many different things collected or brought together
（不同事物的）聚集；堆積

example: an agglomeration of various ethnic and religious groupings
不同種族和宗教的人的集會

NONE: › disapproving formal to make someone more powerful or important
擴大…的權勢；提高…的地位
› an increase in power or importance
（權力、重要性或財富的）擴大，提高，增加

example: He gives a lot of money to charity, but personal aggrandizement/self-aggrandizement is his motive.
他捐了很多錢給慈善機構，但他的動機卻是為了提高個人的地位。

T: › to make a bad situation worse

example: Attempts to restrict parking in the city centre have further aggravated the problem of traffic congestion.
在市中心限制停車的試驗方案使交通擠塞的問題更加嚴重。
The treatment only aggravated the condition.
這種療法反而使病情惡化。
Stop aggravating me, will you!
別再氣我了，好不好！

NONE: › a serious, violent attack on someone
重傷害；嚴重毆打，暴力傷人
› a crime that involves using a weapon or committing another crime while illegally entering a person's house to steal something
惡性侵入住宅罪，惡性暴竊
› informal annoying
惱人的
› formal or specialized law making something worse, such as a crime
加重的

example: I find him really aggravating.
我覺得他這個人真煩人。
Aggravating factors can affect the sentence set by the court.
加重因素將影響法院的審判結果。

C or U: › [ C or U ] UK also informal aggro [ U ] trouble or difficulty

U: › [ U ] formal the act of making something such as a problem or injury worse

example: I've been getting a lot of aggravation at work recently.
最近我工作上事事不順心。
I don't need any more aggravation today.
我今天不想再有更多的煩心事了。
I'd complain to the manager but it's not worth the aggravation.
我本想向經理投訴，可為這事找麻煩不值得。
Rest the affected limb to avoid further aggravation of the condition.
要讓受傷的肢體充分休息，以免情況繼續惡化。

C or U: › something formed by adding together several amounts or things
聚集體，集成體；總數，合計
骨料，集料，粒料（建築用的小石料）

NONE: › total
合計的，總的；總數的
› to combine into a single group or total
使聚集，使積聚

example: They purchased an aggregate of 3,000 shares in the company.
他們總共買了這家公司的3000股股票。
Snowflakes are loose aggregates of ice crystals.
雪花是冰晶鬆散的凝聚體。
Arsenal lost the second game, but got through to the final on aggregate (= adding together the goals in both matches).
兵工廠隊雖然輸了第二場比賽，但是憑藉進球總數進入了決賽。
Volumes of aggregates, cement, and concrete used in the UK will rise this year.
今年英國骨料、水泥和混凝土的使用量都將上升。
The seven companies have an aggregate turnover of £5.2 million.
這七家公司的總營業額為520萬英鎊。

NONE: › in football, the combined number of goals scored by two teams over two or more games
（足球比賽的）總比分

example: Man Utd won the first leg 1-0 and Liverpool won the second 3-1, so the aggregate score was 3-2 to Liverpool.
第一場曼聯隊以1比0贏了利物浦隊，第二場利物浦隊以3比1獲勝，所以兩隊的總比分為3比2，利物浦隊勝出。

NONE: › a person or organization that collects information from the internet pages of other businesses and puts it on a single website
（搜集其他公司資訊並公佈於某一網站的）資訊整合編輯；資訊彙集公司
C1 spoken or physical behaviour that is threatening or involves harm to someone or something
侵略；侵犯；攻擊；挑釁
› forceful playing in sport that is intended to win points
（體育比賽中的）進攻

example: Some types of dog are bred for aggression.
某些品種的狗是養來起攻擊作用的。
an act of aggression
攻擊行為

NONE: B2 behaving in an angry and violent way towards another person
好鬥的；富於攻擊性的；挑釁的
C1 determined to win or succeed and using forceful action to win or to achieve success
積極進取的；有衝勁的；雄心勃勃的
› specialized medical An aggressive disease is one that spreads quickly and has little chance of being cured.
（疾病）惡性的
› specialized medical used to describe a very strong treatment for a serious condition
（對惡性病）積極手段的

example: Men tend to be more aggressive than women.
男性往往比女性更具有攻擊性。
If I criticize him, he gets aggressive and starts shouting.
如果我批評他，他就會尋釁大吵大鬧。
an aggressive election campaign
聲勢浩大的競選活動
Both players won their first-round matches in aggressive style.
兩名選手都以全力以赴、志在必得的打法贏得了第一輪比賽。
The more aggressive the cancer, the further and faster it spreads.
癌症越呈惡性，其發展就越廣越快。
Brain cancer requires aggressive treatment such as surgery.
腦部腫瘤需要採用積極治療手段，比如手術。

NONE: › a person or country that starts an argument, fight, or war by attacking first
侵略者；挑釁者
› unhappy and angry because of unfair treatment
感到委屈的；憤憤不平的

example: He felt aggrieved at not being chosen for the team.
沒有入選該球隊，他感到很委屈。
One aggrieved customer complained that he still hadn't received the book he had ordered several weeks ago.
一位顧客憤憤不平地投訴稱他仍未收到幾週前訂購的書。

NONE: › violent or threatening behaviour, especially between groups of young people
（尤指青少年團夥之間的）鬥毆，鬧事，暴力行為
› trouble or difficulty
煩惱；麻煩

example: There was some aggro between rival fans at the station.
足球比賽對陣雙方的球迷在車站尋釁鬧事。
Why are you being so uncooperative? I don't need this aggro.
你為甚麼這樣不合作？我不想找這種麻煩。
